thesis: Antti Ilmanen argues that there is a critical distinction between objective expected returns, which are derived from long-run empirical data and predictors like starting yields, and subjective expected returns, which are read directly from investor surveys. He aims to clarify this difference to show how subjective expectations can be backward-looking or overly optimistic, particularly during periods of high market valuations, whereas objective measures suggest lower expected returns.
